facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in 1984 in the lower La Amarga Formation alongside the sauropod dinosaur Amargasaurus.
facts.quote: The holotype of Amargasuchus, MACN-N-12, was discovered in 1984 within the lower La Amarga Formation (specifically the Puesto Antigual Member) in association with the dicraeosaurid sauropod dinosaur Amargasaurus.

facts.statement: The species name refers to the La Amarga Formation and the animal's small size.
facts.quote: The name Amargasuchus minor alludes to the La Amarga Formation where the type material was found and the small size of the animal.

facts.statement: The maxilla surface features heavy sculpting, most pronounced along the mid-section.
facts.quote: The surface of the maxilla is ornamented by heavy sculpting, which is most pronounced along the mid-section of the bone.

facts.statement: It inhabited a terrestrial Early Cretaceous environment in the Neuquén basin characterized by braided rivers, lakes, and alluvial plains.
facts.quote: Amargasuchus inhabited a terrestrial paleoenvironment that existed during the Early Cretaceous in the Neuquén basin and was characterized by a system of braided rivers, lakes, and alluvial plains.

facts.statement: It is currently associated with either the clade Pepesuchinae or Itasuchidae.
facts.quote: Today, Amargasuchus is associated with either the clade Pepesuchinae or Itasuchidae, which are nearly identical in some studies.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic studies place it in a polytomy with Caririsuchus, Itasuchus, and Roxochampsa.
facts.quote: In both studies Amargasuchus was recovered as a derived member of its family, with the strict consensus tree placing it in a polytomy consisting of itself, Caririsuchus, Itasuchus and Roxochampsa.

facts.statement: Fossils date from the Barremian to Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Sus restos fósiles se han encontrado en la Formación La Amarga en Argentina y datan de las épocas del Barremiense al Aptiense del Cretácico Inferior.

facts.statement: The time range is estimated from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: It belongs to the subclass Diapsida.
It belongs to the infraclass Archosauromorpha.
It belongs to the superorder Crocodylomorpha.
The type species is A. minor, described by Chiappe in 1988.
It was considered a member of the enigmatic family Trematochampsidae.
facts.quote: Era un miembro de los Trematochampsidae, una enigmática familia de mesoeucrocodilianos.

facts.statement: Taxonomy varies between authors regarding the split of Peirosauridae into subfamilies and their relationships.
facts.quote: The specific nomenclature and taxonomy varies between authors, as some split Peirosauridae into the subfamilies Peirosaurinae and Pepesuchinae, with the latter being similar in its composition to Itasuchidae, itself considered to be the sister group to Peirosauridae.

facts.statement: The formation preserves fossils of the mammal Vincelestes, the abelisaur Ligabueino, and potential tetanuran theropod teeth.
facts.quote: The Puesto Antigual Member also preserves other fossil remains, including several specimens of the mammal Vincelestes, the abelisaur Ligabueino and the teeth of what may be a tetanuran theropod.
